problem: VLN pretraining relies on noisy speaker-generated (back-translated) instructions, but it is unclear whether instruction quality matters at all, or what actually drives the pretraining gains.
motivation: Speaker augmentation instructions are known to be noisy and often unrelated to the paths, yet they help. Understanding whether quality or quantity matters guides cheaper, more scalable augmentation and reveals how much language grounding current R2R agents actually use.
key_idea: Nonsensical (word-shuffled) or irrelevant (mismatched) instructions still preserve most VLN pretraining gains, so the quantity of visual trajectories matters more than instruction quality; a cheap object-word unigram generator (UO) demonstrates this.
insight: On R2R, pretraining SR barely drops with shuffled instructions (HAMT 57.8 to 58.1 with word-shuffle) and mismatched instructions still beat no pretraining (HAMT 51.8 vs 45.8). Augmentation-only pretraining (57.7) matches train+aug (57.8) and beats train-only (53.7), and the gain shows up mainly in the image-only MRM task. Some language is still needed: empty language is worse than no pretraining (27.2 vs 45.8). On RxR, shuffling hurts more (up to -10 SR), suggesting R2R does not demand much language reasoning.
method: Word/sentence shuffling: four noising schemes (shuffle words within sentences, sentence order, both, all words) applied to pretraining and/or fine-tuning instructions while keeping trajectory pairing
Mismatch (permutation): assign instructions to wrong trajectories, either as blocks (all instructions of a trajectory go to the same wrong path) or randomly per instruction
Empty-language pretraining: replace instructions with empty strings for a fraction (0/1/50%) of trajectories

Unigram-Object sampling (UO): a weakly supervised object detector gives top-k objects per panorama along the path; a sliding window (a=3, b=2, k=5) picks objects, and filler words from an R2R unigram model are inserted to match a sampled instruction length. It runs on CPU at 0.01s per instruction
Quality vs quantity: pretrain HAMT on train-only, aug-only, aug subsampled to train size, or both, and compare proxy-task accuracy
Agreement metric: fraction of instructions with the same success outcome between two models; RxR analysis and data cartography (appendix)

numbers_note: Results are SR/SPL/nDTW; ablation-heavy paper, main-text tables give SR only for most settings.
results: Pretraining with word-shuffled instructions loses at most a few SR points on R2R, and mismatched instructions still beat no pretraining (HAMT 51.8 vs 45.8). Aug-only pretraining (57.7 SR) nearly equals train+aug (57.8) and beats train-only (53.7). UO with permuted-all instructions beats train-only pretraining (54.4 vs 53.7 SR). On RxR, shuffling hurts more (up to -10 SR).
limitations: Only R2R/RxR in the discrete Matterport3D graph and English-centric instructions; may not transfer to continuous or outdoor VLN
UO with HAMT alone is worse than train-only pretraining and needs mixing with meaningful mismatched language; still below speaker augmentation (54.4 vs 57.8)
Analysis of two models only; VLN-BERT results are single runs
